# MediaAnnotatedCallouts4

A visual, and what to notice in it.

## When to use it

A screenshot, diagram or dashboard has to be EXPLAINED — the audience needs telling what to look at and in what order.

## Shape

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | G-media |
| Form | annotated |
| Arity | 4 |
| Ground | cream |
| Density | standard, about 460 characters |
| Media | screenshot |
| Focal | media at 520px against a 64px headline (ratio 8.1) |

## Why it holds together

The visual dominates by area because the callouts exist to serve it. Shrink it and the annotations become the subject, which inverts the slide.

## Related kit layout

`ImageContentV3` — ImageContentV3 frames a screenshot; this explains one. The distinct job among the media templates: bleed-steps puts an image beside a list, rel-hub-rings argues FOR a diagram, this one explains a visual the audience is looking at.

## Deviations from the traced source

| What | Source | Here | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| the source's central infographic | a Venn inside a radial dial inside an activation loop | a media slot | Bespoke artwork drawn once for one argument. Only the annotation pattern generalises, and that is what this template is. |

## What the consumer supplies

Copy only. The geometry is measured off a real slide, so when you rebuild it in Claude Design Slides keep the positions and sizes in the preview exactly: change the words, not the grid. Build the text and shapes from the Elements cards, each of which ends with its Slides recipe.

## Origin

Traced from `bank:148` and shipped as canon template `media-annotated-callouts-4`. In the repository its template, `wpp-es-html-deck/canon/templates/media-annotated-callouts-4.html`, is refreshed from this card's preview, and its trace sources (spec, measurements and reference image) are in `authoring/canon-src/media-annotated-callouts-4/`.

# MediaBleedSteps4

Half-bleed image beside a connected sequence.

## When to use it

Three to five named moves in order, where the subject deserves a full-height image.

## Shape

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | G-media (secondary C-sequence) |
| Form | image-bleed |
| Arity | 4 |
| Ground | cream |
| Density | airy, about 330 characters |
| Media | photo |
| Focal | media at 848px against a 64px headline (ratio 13.3) |

## Why it holds together

Measured as width against headline size because the focal element here is an area, not a glyph. The image owns 44% of the canvas; anything less and the slide becomes a list with a picture.

## Related kit layout

`ImageContentV2` — ImageContentV2 pairs the same half-bleed with a single paragraph. This adds the sequence and the connector. Both are worth keeping — v2 when there is one thing to say, this when there are four in order.

## What the consumer supplies

Copy only. The geometry is measured off a real slide, so when you rebuild it in Claude Design Slides keep the positions and sizes in the preview exactly: change the words, not the grid. Build the text and shapes from the Elements cards, each of which ends with its Slides recipe.

# MediaRailCases3

Method, three cases, and what it was worth.

## When to use it

A repeatable process produced three concrete examples with a measurable outcome, and the point is that the cases came from the process.

## Shape

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | G-media (secondary C-sequence) |
| Form | card-grid |
| Arity | 3 |
| Ground | cream, alt |
| Density | dense, about 960 characters |
| Media | screenshot |
| Focal | shot at 250px against a 64px headline (ratio 3.9) |

## Why it holds together

Height against headline size. The images carry the evidence; the rail and the band are navy and orange text and never compete with them.

## Related kit layout

`CardsV3` — CardsV3 is the middle third of this only. The rail is what turns three nice case studies into an argument that they came out of a process rather than luck.

## Deviations from the traced source

| What | Source | Here | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| outcome band colour | grey, which is not in the closed palette | --bg-alt | Reproducing an off-palette fill for fidelity's sake would reproduce a mistake. |
| headline printing through its own subtitle | present | fixed | A defect in the source. |
